``` ::: ::: ## 4. *Data Dictionary* ### *Qualitative Data* 1. name(fct): Name of the student 2. gender(fct): Gender of the student ### *Quantitative Data* 1. total_expenditure_last_week(dbl): Total expenditure of the student the previous week (in Rupees) # 5. *Graphs* ## 1. Graph Why Histogram Shows spending distribution Box Plot Shows spread & comparison by gender Mean Bar Chart Shows average weekly spending difference ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} money_modified2 <- money %>% group_by(gender) %>% summarise(average_expenditure = mean(total_expenditure_last_week, na.rm = TRUE)) money_modified2 %>% gf_col(average_expenditure ~ gender, fill = ~ gender) %>% gf_labs(title = "Which gender has a higher weekly expenditure?", x = "Gender", y = "Average Weekly Expenditure", fill = "Legend: Gender") %>% gf_refine(scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## 2. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} money_modified %>% gf_boxplot(total_expenditure_last_week ~ gender, fill = ~gender, orientation = 'x') %>% gf_labs(title = "What does the distribution of weekly expenditures look like?", x = "Gender", y = "Total Expenditure Last Week", fill = "Legend: Gender") %>% gf_refine(scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Greens")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: perhaps if we had surveyed normal guys it wud be comparable ## 3. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} money%>% gf_histogram(~ total_expenditure_last_week, data = money_modified, fill = "#ff69b4", color = "black") %>% gf_labs(title = "Distribution of expenditure", x = "edd", y = "Number of Crimes") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`.
